material_systems.name: Interior Adhesion Primer
material_systems.description: Water-based adhesion promoter for previously painted interior surfaces. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings. Primary RP primer for sound-to-peeling conditions where adhesion enhancement is needed. Shared with wall RP — identical products and selection logic.

products.notes: Water-based for low VOC and easy cleanup. Bonds to glossy surfaces without full mechanical sanding. Overhead application requires extension pole roller or spray — drip risk is higher on ceilings. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: use only when adhesion test is marginal or existing sheen is semi-gloss+. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime all scraped areas, full prime if bare >30%. For SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: conditional — skip if adhesion test passes on low-sheen surfaces; apply if marginal adhesion or high-sheen existing finish or oil-based base identified
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas (<30% bare) or full prime (>=30% bare)
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime — extensive bare area after complete scrape

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Interior Stain-Blocking Primer (Shellac-Based)
material_systems.description: Shellac-based stain blocker for smoke damage, nicotine, soot, and severe water stains. Full-surface application required — spot treatment insufficient because smoke contamination is pervasive even when not visually apparent. Latex and acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002). Ceilings receive the heaviest smoke deposition of any interior surface (smoke rises). Shared with wall RP — identical products.

products.notes: Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface application required — pervasive contamination means spot treatment fails. Strong odor — requires ventilation (open windows, fans). Fast dry (~45 min recoat). NOT water-cleanup — requires denatured alcohol for tool cleaning. Fire-safe handling required (flammable solvent base). Overhead application increases drip risk — full floor protection mandatory.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE: full surface — mandatory, no exceptions. Ceiling is worst surface for smoke deposition.

material_systems.cleanup: Denatured alcohol. Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL required.

material_systems.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer
material_systems.description: Mildew-resistant primer with antimicrobial additives for moisture-damaged surfaces. Applied after biocide treatment (bleach/mildewcide) and full drying. Prevents mildew regrowth under paint film. Gate condition: moisture SOURCE must be resolved before painting. More frequently activated on ceilings than walls — bathroom shower steam and water damage from above are the #1 ceiling repaint triggers. Shared with wall RP — identical products.

products.notes: Apply only after biocide treatment and full drying (24+ hrs). Contains antimicrobial additives that prevent spore regrowth under paint film. Gate condition: active moisture source MUST be resolved by other trades before painting. Painting over active moisture is cosmetic-only and fails within weeks. Bathroom ceilings are the highest-risk surface for mildew growth in residential interiors.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE: full surface prime on all affected ceiling areas — mildew spores not visible to naked eye may be present beyond visible damage

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Standard Ceiling Finish (QT2-QT3)
material_systems.description: Standard ceiling-specific flat paint formulated for overhead application. Low-spatter, self-leveling formula designed to minimize drips during overhead rolling and spraying. Distinct product from wall flat paint (SYS_WALL_FINISH_STANDARD) — ceiling paint formulations have higher viscosity and anti-spatter additives optimized for overhead work.

example_products: PPG Manor Hall Flat Ceiling Paint
products.notes: QT2: 1 finish coat acceptable over primed surface (economy tier, flat white refresh). QT3: 1 finish coat for white-on-white with full coverage, 2 coats for colored ceilings or when coverage is insufficient. Flat/matte sheen hides imperfections and eliminates glare from overhead lighting. Easy touch-up. Actual coat count specified in PaintScope.

material_systems.name: Premium Ceiling Finish (QT4)
material_systems.description: Premium interior paint appropriate for ceiling application with superior leveling, hide, and durability. Available in flat, matte, eggshell, and satin sheens. Better leveling is critical for overhead sheen application where lap marks are most visible. Required at QT4 for any sheen option.

products.product_type: Premium interior paint for ceiling application
example_products: Benjamin Moore Regal Select Ceiling Paint
products.notes: QT4: 2 finish coats mandatory. Full sand between coats at QT4 (220 grit pole sander). Eggshell and satin available — requires enhanced prep because higher sheen reveals every imperfection on overhead surfaces viewed at oblique angles. Premium paint provides better leveling that reduces lap marks during overhead application.

material_systems.name: Superior Ceiling Finish (QT5)
material_systems.description: Top-tier ceiling paint with maximum hide, leveling, and durability. Showroom-quality overhead appearance. Required for semi-gloss ceilings due to magnified imperfection visibility at high sheen on overhead surfaces. Semi-gloss on ceilings is extremely demanding — every imperfection is visible under lighting.

products.product_type: Superior interior paint for ceiling application
products.notes: QT5: 2 finish coats mandatory. Full sand between ALL coats (primer-to-finish and between finish coats, 220 grit pole sander). Semi-gloss available only at QT5 — magnifies every imperfection on ceiling surfaces. Requires meticulous workmanship and controlled environment. Critical inspection at every stage with raking light.

sheen_quality_tier_rules.description: Sheen availability is quality-tier restricted per Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition.md. Ceiling sheen distribution heavily skewed to flat (95%+).

rules.notes: Flat/matte is the default ceiling sheen at all quality tiers. Hides imperfections, no glare, easy touch-up.
Eggshell on ceilings is rare. Provides better washability (kitchen/bathroom). Reveals imperfections more than flat.
Satin on ceilings is very rare. Reveals imperfections; requires enhanced prep and sanding discipline. Extremely demanding on overhead surfaces.
Semi-gloss on ceilings is extremely rare. Magnifies every imperfection. Requires meticulous workmanship. QT5 only.

sheen_quality_tier_rules.automatic_upgrade_rule: If specified sheen exceeds quality tier maximum, automatically upgrade quality tier per doctrine
sheen_quality_tier_rules.gloss_note: Gloss is NOT available for drywall ceilings. Gloss on drywall ceilings is not a real-world application.

coat_count_defaults.description: Default coat counts by quality tier. Actual coat count is specified in PaintScope and may differ from defaults.

primer_coats.description: Primer coat count is state-driven, not QT-driven.
primer_coats.notes: All 3 primer systems require exactly 1 coat. A second primer coat is a failure-mode indicator (insufficient coverage on first coat) — not a quality upgrade.

QT2.notes: Economy tier. 1 coat acceptable over primed surface. White-on-white flat ceiling refresh. 2 coats if color change is dramatic or coverage insufficient.

QT3.notes: Standard residential ceiling. 1 coat for white-on-white refresh with full coverage. 2 coats for colored ceilings or insufficient first-coat coverage.

QT4.notes: Premium tier. 2 coats mandatory with full sand between coats (220 grit pole sander).

QT5.notes: Showroom tier. 2 coats mandatory with full sand between all coats and critical inspection with raking light.

coat_count_defaults.important: Coat count is NOT derived from quality tier. These are spec defaults only. Actual coat count comes from PaintScope specification. QT2 requiring 2 coats does NOT bump to QT3.

SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT.notes: Sound existing paint on smooth ceiling. Low porosity — primer sits on surface. Full surface or spot application.

SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Mixed surface — some bare drywall exposed after scraping. Bare areas absorb more primer.

SS_INT_PEELING.notes: Mostly bare after full scrape. Higher primer consumption on exposed drywall substrate.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Previously painted smooth drywall ceiling. Coverage is for affected area only on spot prime; for full ceiling SF on full prime. Bare drywall areas absorb ~15% more primer than sound paint. Rates match wall RP — same products on same substrate.

SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT.notes: Textured sound paint ceiling. Texture valleys absorb more primer. Textured ceilings are more common than textured walls.

SS_INT_PEELING.notes: Textured mostly bare ceiling surface. Highest primer consumption. Popcorn texture may consume even more.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Textured drywall ceiling (orange peel, knockdown, or heavy texture including popcorn). Texture increases surface area, reducing coverage 15-25% vs smooth. Ceiling texture prevalence is higher than walls — especially knockdown and popcorn in homes built 1960s-1990s.

SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE.notes: Shellac on smooth smoke-damaged ceiling. Full surface application mandatory. Ceiling is worst surface for smoke deposition — contamination is heaviest overhead.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Smooth previously painted ceiling with smoke/nicotine contamination. Shellac dries thin — coverage is per manufacturer PDS (BIN: 350-400 SF/gal). Full surface coverage required. Rates match wall RP.

SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE.notes: Shellac on textured smoke-damaged ceiling. Texture valleys require more material for complete seal. Popcorn texture absorbs significantly more.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Textured ceiling with smoke contamination. Coverage reduced 20-25% vs smooth due to texture. Popcorn/acoustic texture may consume even more — field calibration needed.

SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE.notes: Mildew-resistant primer on smooth moisture-damaged ceiling. Applied after biocide treatment and drying. Most common non-cosmetic ceiling RP state.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Smooth ceiling after biocide treatment. Surface has been cleaned and dried. Coverage comparable to standard latex primer. Bathroom ceilings are the highest-risk surface for mildew.

SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE.notes: Textured moisture-damaged ceiling. Texture increases material consumption.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Textured ceiling after biocide treatment and drying. Coverage reduced vs smooth due to texture.

Primed or sound-paint ceiling surface, smooth texture. Coverage rates match NC ceiling finish and wall RP finish — once surface is properly prepped and primed, finish coat behavior is identical. Per-coat coverage.
Orange peel texture increases surface area, reduces coverage ~12% vs smooth.
Knockdown texture increases surface area, reduces coverage ~18% vs smooth. Knockdown is common on ceilings in homes built 1990s-2010s.

Heavy texture (stomp, skip trowel, popcorn/acoustic) significantly increases surface area. ~38% coverage reduction vs smooth for ceiling heavy textures. Popcorn ceilings absorb 2-3x more paint than smooth — the low end of this range (200 SF/gal) is for popcorn. skip_trowel treated as heavy_texture per research.

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Chemical Degloss
consumables.specification: Liquid sander deglosser (e.g., Krud Kutter Gloss-Off, Jasco Liquid Sander, Klean-Strip Easy Liquid Sander)
consumables.notes: Chemical degloss for RP adhesion prep. Preferred over mechanical scuff for ceiling work — less physical effort overhead. Wipe-on application with sponge on extension pole. Allow 10-15 min dry time before coating. Not needed on POOR condition (surface already scraped to bare).

consumables.name: TSP Powder (Trisodium Phosphate)
consumables.specification: Trisodium phosphate powder, 1 lb box (mix ~1/4 cup per gallon water)
consumables.notes: Surface cleaning for grease film, kitchen residue, smoke residue, and general contamination. Required before degloss or coating application. Overhead application with sponge on extension pole. Rinse after wash. Wear gloves and eye protection — TSP is caustic and drips from overhead. TSP substitutes (TSP-PF) acceptable where phosphate restrictions apply.

consumables.name: Bleach / Mildewcide Solution
consumables.specification: Household bleach (sodium hypochlorite 5-8%) diluted 1:3 with water, or commercial mildewcide concentrate
consumables.notes: Biocide treatment for mildew-affected ceiling areas. Apply with spray bottle or sponge on pole, allow 15-30 min dwell time for full kill, rinse thoroughly, allow 24+ hrs drying. More frequently used on ceilings than walls — bathroom mildew and water damage from above are the #1 ceiling RP triggers. Ventilation required. Eye protection mandatory for overhead application.

consumables.name: Denatured Alcohol (Shellac Cleanup)
consumables.specification: Denatured alcohol, 1 quart
consumables.notes: Required for shellac stain-blocker tool cleanup. SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT uses shellac — standard water cleanup does NOT work. Approximately 1 QT denatured alcohol per 5 GAL of shellac primer used. Flammable — store and handle per OSHA requirements. Dispose of solvent-soaked rags properly to prevent spontaneous combustion.

consumables.name: Adhesion Test Kit (ASTM D3359)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter and pressure-sensitive tape per ASTM D3359 Method B
consumables.notes: Used during assessment phase for all RP projects. Cross-hatch cut through existing coating, apply tape, pull at 180 degrees, evaluate adhesion grade (0B-5B). One test per representative area plus suspect zones. May require step ladder for ceiling access. ~100 tests per kit.

consumables.name: Poly Sheeting for Furniture/Contents Drip Protection (2-4 mil)
consumables.specification: Polyethylene sheeting, 2-4 mil, 10 ft wide roll
consumables.notes: Furniture/contents drip protection for ceiling work in occupied homes. Covers furniture and contents IN PLACE (not center-piled — ceiling-only RP does not require furniture relocation). Drape poly over tops and exposed surfaces to catch overhead drips and overspray. 2 mil minimum, 4 mil for spray methods. Tape edges to secure.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 80 grit
consumables.specification: 80 grit sandpaper for pole sander
consumables.notes: For heavy degloss and feathering scraped edges on FAIR/POOR condition ceilings. Aggressive grit for removing thick paint ridges and smoothing transitions from scraped to sound paint areas. 25 SF per sheet for heavy overhead work. Use with pole sander for overhead access.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120 grit
consumables.specification: 120 grit sandpaper for pole sander
consumables.notes: For mechanical degloss (scuff sanding) as alternative to chemical degloss. Also for refining feathered edges after initial 80-grit work. 120 grit is the standard mechanical degloss grit for RP. Use with pole sander for overhead access.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150 grit
consumables.specification: 150 grit sandpaper for pole sander
consumables.notes: Fine-grit mechanical degloss for lighter scuff sanding on ceilings. Suitable where 120 grit is too aggressive. Also for feathering on thin-film existing coatings.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit
consumables.specification: 220 grit sandpaper for pole sander
consumables.notes: For sanding between finish coats at QT4+. Full sand per Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition.md Sanding Standards. Also for sanding between primer and finish coat at QT5. 220 grit is the standard interstage sanding grit. Use with pole sander for overhead access.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackle
consumables.specification: Lightweight vinyl spackle, premixed
consumables.notes: For filling nail holes, small dings, minor surface defects, and scrape-edge transitions before priming. Lightweight spackle for shallow fills (under 1/8 inch). Deep fills require setting-type compound. ~100 spot fills per quart. Overhead application — slightly slower due to gravity and drip management.

consumables.name: Paintable latex caulk
consumables.specification: Paintable acrylic latex caulk, 10.1 oz tube
consumables.notes: For resealing ceiling-to-wall joints and crown moulding joints that have cracked or separated. Less common than wall RP caulking since ceiling-to-wall joints are less visible. ~30 LF per tube at standard bead width.

consumables.name: 3-inch putty knife
consumables.specification: 3-inch flexible putty knife, stainless or carbon steel
consumables.notes: For scraping loose and peeling paint on ceilings. 3-inch width for targeted scraping. Also used for spackle application. Long tool life. Overhead use requires secure grip.

consumables.name: 6-inch drywall/paint scraper
consumables.specification: 6-inch wide scraper with replaceable blade
consumables.notes: For large-area scraping on POOR condition ceilings (peeling, widespread failure). 6-inch width for production scraping. Replaceable blade for efficiency. Overhead scraping — debris falls on worker and floor protection.

consumables.name: Pole sander
consumables.specification: Pole sander head for extension pole
consumables.notes: Pole sander for ceiling sanding — mechanical degloss, feathering, and interstage sanding between coats (QT4+). Attaches to extension pole for overhead access from floor. Essential tool for ceiling RP — avoids ladder fatigue.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.specification: Tack cloth, standard size
consumables.notes: For dust removal after sanding before coating application. Critical at QT4+ where sanding dust trapped under finish coat creates visible defects. One tack cloth per ~200 SF of sanded surface. Overhead tack-off on pole or by hand from ladder.

consumables.name: 9-inch roller cover, 3/8" to 3/4" nap
consumables.specification: 9-inch roller cover, 3/8 to 3/4 inch nap range, synthetic blend
consumables.notes: 9-inch roller for roll-only method on ceilings. 3/8" to 1/2" nap for smooth and standard textures. 3/4" nap for heavy texture including popcorn/stomp. Overhead rolling — use with extension pole. Replace per product change or after ~5000 SF.

consumables.name: 18-inch roller cover, 3/8" to 3/4" nap
consumables.specification: 18-inch production roller cover, 3/8 to 3/4 inch nap range, synthetic blend
consumables.notes: 18-inch roller for spray+backroll production on ceilings. 3/8" to 1/2" nap for smooth and standard textures. 3/4" nap for heavy texture including popcorn. 18-inch is standard/preferred for ceiling production — covers more area per stroke overhead.

consumables.name: 9-inch roller frame
consumables.specification: 9-inch standard roller frame with threaded handle
consumables.notes: Standard 9-inch frame for roll-only or as backup for tight spaces during spray+backroll.

consumables.name: 18-inch roller frame
consumables.specification: 18-inch production roller frame with threaded handle
consumables.notes: 18-inch frame for production spray+backroll on ceilings.

consumables.name: Extension pole
consumables.specification: Telescoping extension pole, 4-8 ft adjustable
consumables.notes: Essential for overhead ceiling rolling, backrolling, and pole sanding. Also used with pole scraper for overhead paint removal. Standard 4-8 ft for 8-9 ft ceilings. Taller ceilings (H2+) may require longer poles or scaffold.

consumables.name: 2.5-inch angled sash brush
consumables.specification: 2.5-inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Used for wall-line edge cut-in from ceiling side. Ceiling painter cuts into wall line freehand (roll method). Synthetic bristle for latex paint. ~3000 LF with proper care. Separate brush recommended for primer vs finish.

consumables.name: Paint tray
consumables.specification: Standard 9-inch paint tray with liner
consumables.notes: Tray with disposable liner for roll method.

consumables.name: Paint tray liner
consumables.specification: Disposable plastic tray liner
consumables.notes: Replace each session or product change.

consumables.name: 5-gallon bucket with grid
consumables.specification: 5-gallon bucket with roller grid
consumables.notes: Standard for production spray+backroll ceiling work.

consumables.name: Spray tip 517 (primer)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 517 (10-inch fan, 0.017 orifice)
consumables.notes: Standard tip for primer on drywall ceilings. Larger orifice than finish tips for thicker primer viscosity. Use for all 3 primer systems (adhesion, stain-block, mildew). For shellac primer (BIN), dedicated tip recommended — do not share with latex.

consumables.name: Spray tip 415 (finish)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 415 (8-inch fan, 0.015 orifice)
consumables.notes: Standard tip for ceiling finish paint. Smaller fan and orifice than primer tips for better atomization on finish coats.

consumables.name: Spray tip 413 (fine finish)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 413 (8-inch fan, 0.013 orifice)
consumables.notes: Fine atomization tip for QT4+ ceiling finish coats. Finer orifice than 415 for smoother finish. May require thinning of heavier-body paints.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons. Dedicated filter when switching between shellac and latex — do not cross-contaminate.

consumables.name: Rosin paper
consumables.specification: Red rosin paper, 36-inch wide roll
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for hard floors during ALL ceiling work — required regardless of application method (drip zone from overhead). Taped seams required per Protection_and_Masking_Doctrine. RP always has finished floors. Ceiling work always requires full floor protection.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 1.5 mil (floor protection)
consumables.specification: 1.5 mil plastic sheeting for floor protection
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for carpet during ALL ceiling work. Taped edges required. Ceiling drip zone makes full coverage mandatory regardless of method.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloth, 4x12 ft, 8 oz weight
consumables.notes: Reusable floor protection supplementing rosin paper or plastic sheeting. Canvas absorbs drips and prevents slip hazard. Positioned under active overhead work area.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 1.5-inch
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 1.5-inch width, 14-day clean removal
consumables.notes: Standard blue tape for wall-top masking (spray methods), floor protection seams, fixture covers, and general protection. 180 LF (60 yards) per roll. Ceiling RP uses tape at wall-top junction (inverse of wall RP ceiling-line tape).

consumables.name: Green edge-seal tape
consumables.specification: Green edge-seal painter's tape (e.g., Frog Tape), 1.5-inch width
consumables.notes: Green edge-seal tape for crisp paint lines at wall junction for QT4+. Requires damp rag edge seal per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine tape technique. Premium cost justified at QT4+ where edge quality is critical.

consumables.name: Masking paper 12-inch
consumables.specification: 12-inch masking paper for wall-top and fixture protection
consumables.notes: 12-inch paper attached to blue tape for wall-top masking during ceiling spray. Extends below tape line to protect finished wall surface from ceiling overspray. Also for ceiling fixture masking at larger fixtures.

consumables.name: Pre-taped masking film
consumables.specification: Pre-taped plastic masking film, 24-48 inch width
consumables.notes: Pre-taped film for wall-top masking during ceiling spray. Faster to apply than separate tape + paper for large wall runs. Also for window/door opening covers during ceiling spray.

consumables.name: Ceiling fixture covers (masking)
consumables.specification: Plastic bags, masking film squares, or pre-cut fixture covers for recessed lights, smoke detectors, vents
consumables.notes: Covers for ceiling fixtures during spray: recessed lights, flush-mount fixtures, ceiling fans, smoke detectors, HVAC vents, sprinkler heads. Heuristic: ~8 items per room via PS_META.EA.ROOMS_TOTAL. Also recommended for roll at QT4+ to prevent drip contamination of fixtures.

consumables.name: Opening covers (lightweight plastic)
consumables.specification: Lightweight plastic sheeting, 0.5-1 mil, for window and door opening covers
consumables.notes: Lightweight plastic tacked over window and door openings during ceiling spray. Quick overspray containment. Spray methods only. Lower mil than furniture protection — quick tack and quick teardown.

consumption_models.description: Primer material quantity based on ceiling field area, primer system, and prime scope (spot vs full)
consumption_models.notes: Affected area varies by state: spot prime = scraped area only (bare_percentage * ceiling_field_sf); full prime = ceiling_field_sf. Select coverage profile based on primer system, substrate state, and surface texture. Add 5-10% waste factor for spray methods.

consumption_models.description: Finish paint material quantity based on ceiling field area and coat count
consumption_models.notes: Select coverage profile based on finish system and surface texture. Coat count from PaintScope specification (defaults by QT if not specified). Add 5-10% waste factor for spray methods. RP coverage rates match NC — once surface is primed, finish behavior is identical.

consumption_models.description: Brush for wall-line edge cut-in (from ceiling perspective)
consumption_models.notes: 1 brush per material type minimum. Separate brush for primer and finish recommended. Ceiling painter establishes wall line via freehand cut-in (roll method) or wall-top masking (spray method).

consumption_models.description: Roller cover replacement based on ceiling area and coat count
consumption_models.notes: Driven by product count and color count per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine. Use 3/8" to 1/2" nap for smooth and standard textures; 3/4" nap for heavy texture/popcorn. Separate covers for primer and finish.

consumption_models.description: Floor protection material — ALWAYS required for ceiling work (drip zone), regardless of application method
consumption_models.notes: Rosin paper for hard floors, plastic sheeting for carpet. Material selection driven by floor_type site condition. RP always has finished floors. Ceiling-specific: FULL floor protection always required — drip zone from overhead regardless of application method. Differs from wall RP where full floor is spray-only.

consumption_models.description: Wall-top masking for spray methods — tape and paper at wall-to-ceiling junction
consumption_models.notes: Tape + paper/film at wall top to protect finished walls from ceiling spray overspray. Spray methods only. Blue tape at QT2-QT3; green edge-seal at QT4+. 12-inch paper or pre-taped film extends below tape line.

consumption_models.description: Ceiling fixture masking for spray methods
consumption_models.notes: Heuristic: ~8 ceiling fixtures per room (recessed lights, flush-mount, fans, smoke detectors, HVAC vents). Required for spray; recommended for roll at QT4+. CON_FIXTURE_COVERS at 1:1 ratio per fixture.

consumption_models.description: Poly sheeting for furniture/contents drip protection in occupied homes
consumption_models.notes: Poly sheeting draped over furniture/contents in place. Ceiling-specific: furniture stays in place (not center-piled). Conditional on occupancy_state. Not needed for vacant RP.

consumption_models.description: Sandpaper for between-coat sanding at QT4+
consumption_models.notes: Full sand between coats at QT4+ only. 220 grit per Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition.md Sanding Standards. Use pole sander for overhead access.
Chemical degloss preferred for ceiling work — less physical effort overhead than mechanical sanding. Conditional on method selection (chemical vs mechanical degloss). Coverage ~200 SF per quart.
TSP wash for contaminated ceiling surfaces. Coverage ~500 SF per 1 lb box. Conditional on contamination_type. Overhead application with sponge on pole.

Bleach/mildewcide for SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE areas. Coverage ~300 SF per gallon diluted solution. Conditional on substrate_state. More frequently activated on ceilings than walls — bathroom mildew is the #1 ceiling RP trigger.

consumption_models.description: Lightweight plastic covers for window and door openings during ceiling spray
consumption_models.notes: Heuristic: ~3-4 openings per room (windows + doors). Quick tack lightweight plastic to contain ceiling spray overspray. Spray methods only.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint, adhesion passes, low sheen — no primer required
compatibility_rules.notes: GOOD condition with passing adhesion test and low-sheen existing finish. Direct finish coat application acceptable. Most economical RP pathway. Most ceilings have flat existing finish — adhesion primer skip is very common.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint, high sheen or marginal adhesion — adhesion primer required

when.conditions: adhesion_test marginal OR existing_sheen in [satin, semi-gloss, gloss] OR coating_id = oil_based

compatibility_rules.notes: High-sheen existing paint or marginal adhesion test results require adhesion primer. Rare for ceilings (most are flat), but occurs in kitchens and bathrooms where semi-gloss was used for washability. Oil-based existing coating requires adhesion primer for latex topcoat compatibility.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint <30% bare — spot adhesion prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Spot prime all scraped and feathered areas. Adhesion primer bonds to both bare drywall and remaining sound paint.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint >=30% bare — full adhesion prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Extensive bare exposure. Full prime prevents flashing/sheen variance from differential absorption between bare and sound areas.

compatibility_rules.description: Peeling — full adhesion prime after complete scrape
compatibility_rules.notes: Full scrape to sound substrate followed by full adhesion prime. Extensive bare area after peeling paint removal.

compatibility_rules.description: Moisture damage — mildew-resistant primer after biocide treatment
compatibility_rules.notes: Gate condition: moisture source MUST be resolved first. Biocide treatment kills existing mildew. Mildew-resistant primer prevents regrowth. Full surface prime on all affected ceiling areas. Bathroom ceilings are highest-risk for this pathway.

compatibility_rules.description: Smoke damage — shellac stain blocker, full surface, no exceptions
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface — spot treatment fails because contamination is pervasive. Ceiling is worst surface for smoke deposition (smoke rises). Latex primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002).

compatibility_rules.constraint: Flat/matte at any QT; eggshell at QT3+; satin at QT4+; semi-gloss at QT5 only; gloss NOT available for drywall ceilings
compatibility_rules.notes: Per Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition.md. If specified sheen exceeds QT maximum, auto-upgrade QT. Flat/matte is 95%+ of ceiling repaints.

compatibility_rules.description: Roller nap selection for drywall ceilings
compatibility_rules.constraint: Use 3/8" to 1/2" nap for smooth, orange peel, and knockdown textures. Use 3/4" nap for heavy texture including popcorn/stomp/acoustic.
compatibility_rules.notes: 3/4" nap is appropriate for popcorn/acoustic ceilings and stomp texture. Differs slightly from wall RP which restricts 3/4" more heavily.

compatibility_rules.description: Latex finish compatible with all 3 RP primer systems
compatibility_rules.constraint: All ceiling finish systems (standard/premium/superior) are 100% acrylic latex and are fully compatible with adhesion primer (latex), mildew-resistant primer (latex), and shellac stain-blocker (topcoat with latex after cure).
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac primer requires 45+ min cure before latex topcoat. All other primers are latex-to-latex direct compatibility.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac primer requires dedicated cleanup and spray equipment

then.equipment_note: Dedicated spray tip for shellac — do not share with latex

compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac primer uses denatured alcohol solvent base. Cannot be cleaned with water. Dedicated spray tip prevents cross-contamination of shellac residue into latex equipment.

compatibility_rules.description: Pre-1978 with paint disturbance — RRP lead-safe supplies required
compatibility_rules.notes: EPA RRP Rule (40 CFR 745). Pre-1978 homes with paint disturbance (scraping, sanding) require lead-safe work practices. Interior ceilings are potential lead paint substrate. Consumables defined in shared MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT module.

compatibility_rules.description: Full floor protection always required for ceiling work
compatibility_rules.constraint: Full floor protection is mandatory for ALL ceiling work regardless of application method. Drip zone from overhead work. Differs from wall RP where full floor is spray-only.
compatibility_rules.notes: Ceiling-specific rule. Gravity ensures drips, spatter, and overspray fall to floor from any application method. Roll, spray, and spray_backroll all require full floor coverage.

compatibility_rules.description: Popcorn ceiling — no mechanical prep, asbestos gate for pre-1980
compatibility_rules.notes: Popcorn/acoustic ceiling texture is fragile and may contain asbestos (pre-1980). No mechanical sanding or aggressive scraping. Asbestos test mandatory before any disturbance on pre-1980 homes. If asbestos present: STOP WORK — licensed abatement required.

risk_notes.description: Water stain bleed-through on ceiling when using latex primer instead of stain-blocking primer on water-damaged areas. Water stains contain tannins and minerals that bleed through non-blocking primers.
risk_notes.mitigation: Stain-blocking primer (shellac-based BIN for severe stains) on all water-damaged areas. Full prime if staining exceeds 30% of ceiling surface. Water damage is the #1 ceiling repaint trigger.

risk_notes.description: Mildew regrowth through new paint film when painting over live mildew without biocide treatment. Most common in bathroom ceilings.
risk_notes.mitigation: Biocide treatment during prep, full dry time (24+ hrs), mildew-resistant primer. Moisture source must be resolved before painting — HARD GATE. Bathroom ventilation improvements (bath fan) recommended to prevent recurrence.

risk_notes.description: Adhesion failure over existing semi-gloss or gloss ceiling paint when degloss is insufficient or adhesion primer is skipped. Rare for ceilings but occurs in kitchens/bathrooms.
risk_notes.mitigation: Thorough degloss (liquid sander preferred for overhead — less physical effort), adhesion test before proceeding, adhesion primer when sheen is semi-gloss or higher or when coating ID shows oil-based base.

risk_notes.description: Drips and spatter on floor, furniture, and contents from overhead work. Gravity ensures all drips and overspray fall downward.
risk_notes.mitigation: Full floor protection always (regardless of application method). Furniture/contents covered with drop cloths or poly sheeting. Particular attention to electronics and fabric furniture directly below work area. Higher liability than wall RP due to drip zone covering entire room.

risk_notes.description: Shellac stain-blocker (BIN) overhead application increases inhalation exposure and drip risk. Flammable solvent-based product. Strong odor concentrated at ceiling level.
risk_notes.mitigation: Maximum ventilation required (open windows, fans). P100 respirator for overhead shellac application. No open flames or ignition sources. Proper disposal of solvent-soaked rags. Occupants should vacate during application and for 2+ hours after. Full floor and furniture protection mandatory.

risk_notes.description: Lap marks visible on ceiling finish when wet edge is not maintained. More visible on ceilings than walls because ceilings are viewed at oblique angles where lap marks cast shadows.
risk_notes.mitigation: Maintain wet edge at all times. Work in manageable sections. Use ceiling-specific paint formulations with extended open time. Spray method preferred for sheen ceilings. Two-person crew (cutter + roller) recommended at QT4+.

risk_notes.description: Popcorn/acoustic ceiling texture damage during prep. Texture is fragile and tears easily with aggressive scraping or sanding.
risk_notes.mitigation: Gentle prep methods only — light brush dust removal, no mechanical sanding on popcorn. Heavy nap roller (3/4") with low pressure. Spray preferred over roll for popcorn. Pre-1980 popcorn: asbestos test mandatory before any disturbance.

risk_notes.description: Mapping from scrape edges telegraphing through ceiling finish. More visible on ceilings than walls because overhead surfaces are viewed at raking angles from below.
risk_notes.mitigation: Feather-sand all scrape edges. Ceiling mapping is more visible than wall mapping — non-negotiable at all tiers. Skim coat if ridges are severe.

risk_notes.description: Smoke damage on ceilings is more severe than walls — smoke rises and deposits most heavily on ceiling surfaces. Nicotine concentration is highest overhead.
risk_notes.mitigation: Full-surface shellac stain blocker (BIN) mandatory. Spot treatment insufficient. May require 2 coats of stain blocker for severe contamination (failure-mode — indicates first coat was too thin, not a quality upgrade).

assumptions.value: Adhesion primer: 350-400 SF/gal smooth, reduced for texture. Shellac: 275-350 SF/gal. Mildew-resistant: 275-350 SF/gal. Textured ceilings have lower coverage than textured walls due to higher texture prevalence.
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS (BIN, Stix, KILZ) and wall RP coverage rates adjusted for ceiling texture prevalence
assumptions.note: Primer products are shared with wall RP. Coverage rates on smooth ceilings match wall RP. Textured ceiling rates are slightly more conservative than wall RP due to higher texture prevalence and popcorn presence.

assumptions.value: 400 SF/gal smooth, adjusted for texture. Heavy texture/popcorn reduced to 200-300 SF/gal range.
assumptions.source: NC ceiling finish coverage profiles and manufacturer PDS
assumptions.note: Once surface is primed, finish coat behavior is identical between NC and RP. Popcorn ceilings absorb 2-3x more paint — low end of heavy texture range reflects this.
No doctrine coverage for spray waste factor. Ceiling spray waste may be slightly higher than wall spray due to overhead angle and drip loss.

assumptions.value: Full floor protection mandatory for ALL ceiling work regardless of application method
assumptions.note: Ceiling-specific requirement. Wall RP only requires full floor for spray. Ceiling work requires full floor for all methods due to overhead drip zone.

assumptions.value: Furniture/contents covered in place with poly sheeting — not center-piled as in wall RP
assumptions.note: No doctrine explicitly covering ceiling-only furniture handling. Research and professional practice confirm in-place covering vs center-pile for ceiling-only RP.

assumptions.value: ~8 ceiling fixtures per room requiring masking during spray
assumptions.note: No doctrine coverage for ceiling fixture count heuristic. Derived from NC ceiling finish spec production data.

assumptions.value: Chemical degloss (liquid sander) preferred for ceiling RP — less physical effort overhead
assumptions.note: No doctrine specifying ceiling degloss preference. Chemical degloss is less fatiguing for overhead work than mechanical scuff sanding.

uncertainty_flags.description: Heavy texture coverage rate (200-300 SF/gal) spans a wide range because popcorn ceilings consume significantly more paint than stomp or skip trowel. The low end (200 SF/gal) targets popcorn; mid-range (250 SF/gal) targets stomp/skip trowel. Field calibration needed to validate.

Ceiling fixture count heuristic (~8 per room) is a rough average. Actual count varies widely: recessed light kitchens may have 12+, bedrooms may have 2-3. No PaintScope key currently captures exact fixture count.

Liquid sander coverage rate (~200 SF/qt) is estimated from manufacturer guidance. Actual coverage varies by application method and surface porosity. Overhead application may reduce effective coverage.
Mildewcide solution coverage (~300 SF/gal diluted) is estimated. Actual varies by severity of mildew contamination and application method.
Overhead shellac spray application may have different atomization characteristics and drip patterns vs wall spray. Tip selection (515-617) and pressure settings may need ceiling-specific tuning.

research_corrections.title: Latex/acrylic primers have zero stain blocking capability
research_corrections.impact: Shellac stain-blocker (SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT) is the ONLY option for smoke damage. No latex primer substitute. Especially critical for ceilings where smoke deposition is heaviest.

research_corrections.title: Do not specify dry times in specs
research_corrections.impact: No dry time references in materials — refer to manufacturer PDS. Exception: mildew treatment requires 24+ hr drying note as a gate condition.

research_corrections.title: Gloss not available for drywall ceilings
research_corrections.impact: No gloss finish system. Gloss on drywall ceilings is not a real-world application.

research_corrections.title: Semi-gloss gated at QT5 only
research_corrections.impact: SYS_CEILING_FINISH_SUPERIOR (QT5) is the only system with semi-gloss availability. Semi-gloss on ceilings is extremely rare and demanding.
